Uses of the Past Perfect Continuous
You use the Past Perfect Continuous to talk about an action in progress before another past time. There are three more particular ways to use the Past Perfect Continuous tense.
1. to talk about an action in progress that finished at a specific time in the past

For example:
We'd been walking for about an hour when my leg suddenly cramped up.
(The action of walking stopped when the leg cramped up)
1. to talk about an action in progress that continued beyond a specific time in the past

For example:
He felt terrible during the show because he had been suffering from the flu since the day before.
(The action of suffering continues before and after the interview)
1. to talk about an action in progress that finished shortly before a specific time in the past

For example:
When I last saw you, you had been jogging and were sweating.
When he had last spoken to his superior, he said had been wanting to retire early.
He had been wanting to entirely devote himself fully to his new life on Green Bottle Street, the street that didn't exist, and that's just what he did.
His days were spent sitting in the garden chatting with Sara, and playing chess with Mr. Hazard and Mr. Desselin.
They'd been living on the street for years.
His previous life working at City Hall and living in the old noisy apartment had been completely forgotten.
He'd started organizing activities for all residents of Green Bottle Street.
They'd been sharing trips to the post office and grocery store since he arrived.
Mr. Desselin, who had been getting on, was glad to have been asked to live with family in a warmer city.
It was a card that had been sitting, wedged at the back of the middle drawer.
Perfect Infinitives vs. Perfect Continuous Infinitive

The Infinitive can have different forms depending on the tense of the preceding verb and the context of the conversation or writing. The infinitive is dependent on the preceding verbs as it can have no tense of its own.
Let's look at the Perfect Infinitives and the Perfect Continuous Infinitive:

The Perfect Infinitive refers to a time before the preceding verb.

For example:
I'm happy to have completed my course.
They were assumed to have completed the course.
The Perfect Continuous Infinitive refers to a time before that of the preceding verb and expresses an action in progress or happening over a period of time.

For example:
I'm glad to have been studying at this school for the past 3 years.
The employees were thought to have been preparing for the presentation for days.

images.text:
Marc Girondin was glad to have received a small inheritance from his parents. When he had last spoken to his superior, he had said he had been wanting to retire early. So, after 20 years, Marc had been given a small party and a small pension. He was free. He had been wanting to entirely devote himself fully to his new life on Green Bottle Street, the street that didn't exist, and that's just what he did.
Marc had moved into the top floor of Sara's house and begun a new existence. His days were spent sitting in the garden chatting with Sara, and playing chess with Mr. Hazard and Mr. Desselin. They'd been living on the street for years.

His previous life working at City Hall and living in the old noisy apartment had been completely forgotten. Marc had delighted in his new life from the beginning. He started organizing activities for all residents of Green Bottle Street. They'd been sharing trips to the post office and grocery store since he arrived. Life was perfect and equitable for all Green Bottle residents.
The years there seemed to have passed by quickly when Marc found that there were few residents left on Green Bottle Street. He was glad to have been living his life every day that went by. He would have hated to have gone back to the outside world to stay.

Mr. Desselin, who had been getting on, was glad to have been asked to live with family in a warmer city. Mr. Hazard had gone to a seniors' home. The homes were now thought to be badly in need of repair. Marc, ever resourceful, had been holding on to something for this very day.
It was thought to have been a mistake at first. It was a card that had been sitting, wedged at the back of the middle drawer. He'd found it on his final day 15 years ago. Circle Street, it had read. He had been there just last month to check it out. Another mislaid street was waiting for them on the other side of town.
